facts.raw_span: a red tumor on her right upper arm that enlarged over 6 months
The lesion initially started as a small cutaneous nodule
no history of local trauma or insect bite
a 6 × 6-cm protuberant, thick-walled, and well-defined red bullalike tumor on the right upper arm
a nontender, firm-to-hard nodule was palpated
no regional lymphadenopathy
Hematologic, biochemical, and urinalysis tests were normal
multilocular spaces below the epidermis and a solid tumor present in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance
basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis and dilated lymphatic vessels in the dermis above the tumor

concepts.why: The presence of basophilic cells, shadow cells, and multilocular spaces with a chalky-white cut surface is characteristic of pilomatrixoma.
The firm-to-hard nodule and well-defined red tumor are consistent with dermatofibroma, although the lack of history of trauma is not typical.
The rapid growth and protuberant nature of the tumor, along with the presence of a firm nodule, could suggest keratoacanthoma, but the histological findings are not typical.
The well-defined red tumor with a firm nodule and multilocular spaces could be consistent with cylindroma, although the location and size are not typical.
The presence of basophilic cells and dilated lymphatic vessels could suggest spiradenoma, although the clinical presentation is not typical.
